citation_policy.scheme: two grades, used for every literature value in this organ and worded the same way as the other digestive-tract organs of this project

levels.VALUE GRADE B: 数值 B 级。The number came from a search snippet that was NOT retained in the deliverables, and it was NOT checked against the paper. A reader cannot reproduce the retrieval from anything shipped here. Treat every such number as unverified.
levels.PAPER-IDENTITY GRADE A: 论文身份 A 级。The journal, volume, DOI or PMID printed next to the number is checkable, so a reader can go and look the value up themselves.

citation_policy.rule: EVERY numeric literature value in this organ is VALUE GRADE B with PAPER-IDENTITY GRADE A. None is grade A on the value. A reference printed next to a number is a POINTER TO WHERE TO CHECK IT, not evidence that this project checked it.
citation_policy.downgrade_note: An earlier draft of this file labelled four references (surface area, haustral manometry, HAPC statistics, SCFA concentrations) as primary sources read during the build. That label was not supportable from anything in the deliverables and has been removed: no citation in this organ now claims any retrieval action, and all of them sit at VALUE GRADE B.
citation_policy.numbers_this_project_produced_itself: Anything labelled MEASURED or DERIVED (mesh, centreline, segment lengths, taenia and haustra geometry, Murray residuals, clearances, velocities, reflux audit, motion audit, single-cell expression) was computed here, and the code that produced it ships in the tools bundle.

crypt.villi: ABSENT -- the colonic mucosa is flat. There are crypts of Lieberkuehn and no villi anywhere in the colon. This is the single biggest structural difference from the small intestine and is why the colon absorbs over a far smaller area.
crypt.magnification_note: the crypt is modelled at its real micrometre size and then shown at a DECLARED 60x magnification -- the same factor the small-intestine page uses for its villus-crypt unit, so the two microscopic views are directly comparable at a glance.

surface_area.source: Helander HF, Faendriks L. Surface area of the digestive tract - revisited. Scand J Gastroenterol 2014;49:681-9, doi:10.3109/00365521.2014.898326 (PMID 24694282): total mucosal surface ~32 m2, of which ~2 m2 large intestine; microvillar amplification in the colon ~6.5x; villi plus microvilli amplify the small intestine 60-120x

surface_area.measured_note: the 105047 mm2 above is the area of the SEGMENTATION SURFACE of this subject at 1.5 mm voxel resolution. It is the serosal envelope of a partly collapsed colon, NOT the mucosal area: it resolves neither haustra at full depth nor crypts, and it is about 19x smaller than the published 2 m2 mucosal figure. The two numbers measure different things and must not be compared directly.

mass_movement.trigger: gastrocolic response -- a meal (and waking) raises the rate of high-amplitude propagating contractions
mass_movement.source: high-amplitude propagated contractions: 100-200 mmHg, 20-30 s, median 6 per 24 h (range 2-24); velocity 0.71 +/- 0.05 cm/s with proximal continuing waves 0.79 +/- 0.05 cm/s (range 0.29-1.50 cm/s); HAPC definition >=65 mmHg propagating >=30 cm. J Neurogastroenterol / AJP-GI 2020 ajpgi.00386.2019 and the HAPC literature

sequence: rectal filling by a mass movement
rectal wall distension detected by stretch receptors
recto-anal inhibitory reflex: internal anal sphincter relaxes, external sphincter contracts (sampling)
urge; voluntary control of the external anal sphincter and puborectalis
if deferred, rectal accommodation; if permitted, straining and evacuation
defecation.measured_note: the rectal lumen volume above is computed from THIS SUBJECT's measured rectal radius profile; it is a geometric volume of the segmentation, not a barostat measurement

azoreduction.mechanism: bacterial azoreductases cleave the azo bond; the parent drug passes the small intestine intact and is only activated where the bacterial load is high
azoreduction.why_it_matters: this is the design principle of colon-targeted prodrugs: the colon is used as the activation compartment

watersheds.griffiths_point: the splenic flexure sits in the SMA/IMA watershed. It is the classical site of ischaemic colitis because it depends on the marginal artery for collateral flow between two separate arterial territories.
watersheds.sudeck_point: the rectosigmoid junction is the second watershed, between the last sigmoid artery and the superior rectal artery.

route_comparison.sublingual: oral mucosa -> lingual/facial veins -> internal jugular -> SVC: systemic, NO hepatic first pass
route_comparison.gastric_and_upper_gi: stomach and small intestine -> portal vein -> LIVER: full hepatic first pass
route_comparison.upper_rectum: superior rectal vein -> inferior mesenteric vein -> portal vein -> LIVER: full first pass
route_comparison.lower_rectum: middle and inferior rectal veins -> internal iliac vein -> IVC: systemic, BYPASSES the hepatic first pass
route_comparison.caveat: the fraction of a suppository dose that escapes first pass depends on how high in the rectum it dissolves and on anastomoses between the superior and the middle rectal veins. NO bypass fraction is computed in this project; the three routes are shown as topology, not as a pharmacokinetic prediction.
